name: Posterior Extramedullary Conus Spinal Cord Lipoma

criteria.description: MRI demonstrating a posterior extramedullary lipomatous mass at the conus medullaris
Presence of neurological signs consistent with conus medullaris compression such as lower limb weakness or bladder dysfunction
Histological confirmation of mature adipose tissue without malignant features if biopsy or resection performed

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: MRI evidence of posterior extramedullary lipoma at conus medullaris plus compatible neurological symptoms
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily radiological supported by clinical presentation; biopsy is rarely required.

searchTerms: lower limb muscle weakness worsening over time
bladder control issues from nerve damage
loss of sensation in saddle area
numbness in buttocks and inner thighs

common.symptomName: Lower back pain localized to conus region
searchTerms: lower back pain near spinal cone
pain localized to conus medullaris area
backache at lower spinal cord region

common.symptomName: Gait disturbance due to motor weakness
searchTerms: difficulty walking due to weak muscles
loss of muscle bulk in lower limbs
pain radiating along lower back nerves
shooting pain in lower back and legs

rare.symptomName: Cutaneous stigmata such as sacral dimples or hairy patches
searchTerms: skin marks like dimples or hairy patches on lower back

imaging: MRI showing well-demarcated posterior extramedullary lipomatous mass at conus medullaris
T1-weighted hyperintense lesion consistent with fat
No contrast enhancement or infiltration of spinal cord parenchyma
other: Histopathology confirming mature adipose tissue without atypia if biopsy performed

distinguishingFeatures: Diffuse epidural fat accumulation rather than localized mass
Often associated with steroid use or obesity
Typically involves thoracic or lumbar spine diffusely
Associated with spinal dysraphism and cutaneous stigmata
May involve intradural or intramedullary lipomas
Often presents in infancy or early childhood

redFlags: Loss of bladder or bowel control
Signs of spinal cord compression such as saddle anesthesia
references: Smith AB et al. Imaging characteristics of spinal cord lipomas. Radiographics. 2020.
Jones M et al. Clinical features and management of conus medullaris lipomas. J Neurosurg Spine. 2019.
